guard_streams.source: Monitoring compliance with the net neutrality rules
guard_streams.write_limit: Net-neutrality monitoring concerns traffic treatment and compliance, not physical network availability or measured fixed-broadband speed at a parcel.

facts.detail: Ofcom monitors and ensures compliance with UK net-neutrality rules.
Ofcom is required to publish an annual monitoring report.
Ofcom's review found the framework generally worked well.
The framework supported consumer choice.
It enabled content providers to deliver services to consumers.
Ofcom identified areas where clearer guidance was needed.
Revised guidance supports efficient network management and innovation.
The guidance applies to mobile and broadband providers.
The 2025 document is Ofcom's ninth annual monitoring report.
The 2024 and 2023 documents were the eighth and seventh annual reports.

guard_streams.source: Clarification to Ofcom's net neutrality guidance on public interest exceptions
guard_streams.write_limit: Traffic-management exceptions and harmful-content blocking rules do not verify broadband coverage, orderability or parcel-measured performance.

facts.detail: Ofcom published the clarification on 20 July 2026.
Net neutrality supports users controlling what they see and do online.
UK rules require equal treatment of broadband and mobile traffic.
Providers should not prioritise, slow or block content to favour some services.
Ofcom is responsible for monitoring compliance.
Ofcom reviewed the UK framework in October 2023.
Guidance permits certain public-interest traffic-management exceptions.
Prior examples included fraudulent and intimate-image-abuse content.
The clarification states that the exception list is not exhaustive.
Ofcom considers blocking case by case, including proportionality, targeting, evidence and complaint mechanisms.
